newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila nabs 21 Chinese off shoal, Beijing protests.
newsitem.headline: Manila nabs 21 Chinese off shoal, Beijing protests.

text.p: The Philippine Navy has arrested 21 Chinese fishermen off a disputed rock in the South China Sea, and China has demanded their release, saying they were in Chinese territory, officials said on Tuesday.

The fishermen were apprehended 11 km (seven miles) southeast of the Scarborough Shoal on May 20 and were being detained by the coast guard at nearby Subic freeport, navy spokesman Commander Salvador Cuba said.
The navy had impounded the vessel while it questioned the crew, he said.
"They were apprehended for entering our territory," Cuba added.
The incident coincides with talks in Beijing between senior officials of the two countries aimed at easing tensions over rival claims for the tiny islands and rocky outcrops in the South China Sea.

The Chinese embassy has complained to the Foreign Ministry over the arrests and demanded the release of the fishermen, saying they had the right to fish in the area because it is Chinese territory, a senior Filipino diplomat told reporters.
The embassy also asked that its officials be allowed to see the fishermen, the diplomat said.
Beijing insists all the islands, reefs and rocky outcrops in the South China Sea historically belong to China and has cited centuries-old documents to back its claim.
The contested shoal, a 16-km (10-mile) rock formation that almost disappears at high tide, lies about 200 km (125 miles) west of the Philippines' Zambales island.
Manila says the rocks are within its exclusive economic zone and that it has sovereignty over them.
"We have also the right to arrest them because they are within the Philippine territory," the Filipino diplomat said.

Beijing also protested to Manila earlier this month after Filipino fishermen raised their country's flag over the shoal. That occurred after Philippine navy vessels drove a Chinese expedition of amateur radio operators away from the shoal.
Last month, Manila accused Beijing of sending armed naval ships near islands that both nations claims in the potentially oil-rich Spratlys group, well south of the Scarborough Shoal.
The Spratley islands and reefs are also claimed wholly or in part by the Taiwan, Malaysia, Vietnam and Brunei.
